Melissa McDonough

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 38, Harris County, Texas · Open seat

Realtor and real estate brokerage owner

Melissa McDonough is a Realtor from Tomball who has sold real estate in the Houston area for about 30 years. She was the Democratic nominee for Texas' 38th Congressional District in 2024 and lost to Republican Wesley Hunt. In 2026 she won the Democratic primary outright on March 3 with 51.6% of the vote, and in the November 3 general election she faces Jon Bonck (R) and Alex McMenemy (G) for a seat with no incumbent.

Where McDonough stands

Checks and balances / role of Congress
Says that restoring checks and balances is the first priority of Congress, ahead of platform goals on health care, the economy or affordability.
Cost of living / affordability
Says the war's effects on shipping routes and energy prices are being passed on to consumers. She lists food pantry shortages, screwworm effects on farmers and possible Medicare coverage changes as cost concerns.
Housing
Calls housing affordability and stability in TX-38 a priority. She ties them to supply shortages and rising costs, and says renters, working families and low-income households are struggling.
Immigration and border
Proposes streamlining the immigration process instead of spending on border barriers, and addressing root causes in Latin America. Argues that long backlogs can increase illegal immigration.
Guns
Supports Ethan's Law, secure firearm storage, stronger background checks and expanded mental-health care. Opposes banning guns and says these measures protect the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding Texans.

Background

  • 2026: Won the Democratic primary for U.S. House TX-38 (51.6%), defeating Marvalette Hunter and Theresa Courts
  • 2024: Democratic nominee for U.S. House TX-38; lost the general election to Wesley Hunt (R), receiving 37.2%
  • Realtor and real estate brokerage owner, about 30 years in the Houston area
  • Harris County election worker roles: presiding judge, ballot board, signature verification, central count
  • Volunteer lobbyist on Capitol Hill for consumer protection and health care issues
  • Born in Marietta, Ohio
